A `div` with an `onClick` works with a mouse and with nothing else. People who use a keyboard, a switch or a screen reader cannot trigger it, because Enter and Space do nothing on a `div`.

The best answer is usually a `button`: it takes the focus and turns Enter and Space into a click by itself. If it has to be another element, add `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp` or `onKeyPress`.

Not checked: components, controls such as `button`, `input`, `select` and `a` with an `href`, elements with `aria-hidden`, and elements with `role="presentation"` or `role="none"`.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```jsx
const row = <div onClick={openDetails}>{item.name}</div>;
const more = <a onClick={loadMore}>Load more</a>;
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
const row = <button onClick={openDetails}>{item.name}</button>;

const card = (
  <div role="button" tabIndex={0} onClick={openDetails} onKeyDown={openOnEnter}>
    {item.name}
  </div>
);
```
